specs.description: The 540-ds MCP server gives an AI agent a registry of read-only tools (mcp/tools/index.ts) to query the design system while it assembles a piece: get-design-guide, list-templates, get-rules, get-template, get-patterns, get-template-stops, list-components, search-components, get-component, get-component-docs, get-component-stories, get-tokens and search-images. Every listed tool is annotated read-only. get-design-guide returns src/docs/diseno.md without the note for editors. list-templates lists every piece type in PIECE_TYPES with what it is, its triggers and the tools that have data for it, and the pieceType enum of the template tools is taken from the same source (PIECE_TYPE_IDS). Only talks are served: any other piece type is refused. get-rules returns the talk rules, also when no pieceType is given. list-components filters by level. get-component returns props with their types, defaults and descriptions, finds parts and tag names, and, when it finds none, suggests up to five component or part names only where the normalized name contains the normalized query, or the normalized query, longer than 2 characters, contains the name; a typo such as "Buton" gets no suggestion. get-component-docs returns the component's sheet in Markdown. get-component-stories includes story code only when asked. search-components is a literal text match, not a match by meaning: it folds the query (accents removed, lowercase), splits it into terms longer than one character, and scores each term found as literal text in the component and part names (10), their descriptions (4), the prop names and descriptions (2) and the docs (1 per occurrence, at most 5), returning the 8 highest-scoring components; a Spanish word such as "cita" finds a component only because its docs are in Spanish and contain that word. get-tokens filters by category and text. get-template gives the shell and the index of stops without their code. get-template-stops returns each stop's code with its helpers and sample assets, and reports ids it does not know. search-images finds photos by theme, applies filters and skips photos already used. get-patterns filters by need and points to stops.
specs.name: MCP tools

specs.description: The 540-ds MCP server is reached over Streamable HTTP through a stateless, Web-standard handler (mcp/http.ts), and the local server and the Firebase function bridge Node's HTTP objects to it (mcp/node-adapter.ts). createServer(metadata) builds an MCP server named 540-ds whose instructions are metadata.instructions.content, and registers every tool of the registry annotated read-only. handleMcpRequest(request, metadata) answers OPTIONS with 204 and open CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin *); answers any method other than POST, such as GET or DELETE, with 405, a JSON-RPC error and the header Allow: POST, OPTIONS; and gives each POST its own server and transport with no session: the answer is plain JSON with no Mcp-Session-Id header, initialize returns the server info and instructions, and tools can be listed and called without a session. Every answer carries the open CORS headers. toWebRequest(req, origin, rawBody) turns a Node request into a Web Request with the same method, the URL resolved against origin and every header, a repeated header keeping all its values; a GET or HEAD request carries no body; otherwise the body is rawBody when it is given, else it is streamed from the Node request. sendWebResponse(res, response) writes the response's status, headers and whole body to the Node response.
specs.name: MCP transports

specs.description: The server side of the island runtime (src/runtime/server.ts and src/runtime/islands.ts) turns design-system components into static HTML that the client runtime later hydrates. registryOf collects, from the modules it is given, every export whose name starts with a capital letter and whose value is a component (a function, or an object with $$typeof), keyed by its export name; other exports are left out. ISLAND_TAG is 'ds-island' and SLOT_TAG is 'ds-slot'. renderIsland(registry, {name, props, id, slots}) throws '540-ds: component "<name>" is not registered' when the registry has no component of that name; otherwise it renders the component with its revived props to HTML, with id as the prefix of every id the component generates with useId, and wraps that HTML as <ds-island data-c="<name>" data-id="<id>" data-p="<props as JSON>">, escaping &, " and < in those attributes. revive turns encoded props back into props: an object with a string $slot becomes a Slot rendered as <ds-slot data-s="<slot id>"> holding that slot's HTML, and renderIsland throws '540-ds: slot "<slot id>" has no HTML' when its slots have no entry for it; an object with a string $el becomes an element of that HTML tag when the name starts with a lowercase letter, otherwise of the registered component of that name, with its revived p as props, and revive throws '540-ds: component "<name>" is not registered; include its island' when no such component is registered; any other array, object or plain value is revived member by member and keeps its shape. renderStatic(element, id) renders an element the same way, with id as the prefix of its generated ids, without the island wrapper. renderToString(element, {identifierPrefix}) renders it with identifierPrefix as that prefix, or none when it is absent, and renderToStaticMarkup is the same function.
specs.name: Island server rendering

specs.description: The design tokens module (src/tokens/breakpoints.ts and src/tokens/manifest.ts) names the system's screen breakpoints and lists its tokens for the Foundations documentation pages. BREAKPOINTS is {tablet: 600, desktop: 1024}, in px; DESIGN_WIDTHS, the widths each range is designed at, is {mobile: 375, tablet: 768, desktop: 1440}; MEDIA holds, for tablet and for desktop, the media query '(min-width: <its breakpoint>px)', so tablet is '(min-width: 600px)' and desktop is '(min-width: 1024px)'. The manifest holds token names, labels and descriptions but no values: colorPrimitives is a list of groups, each with a title, a description and items naming a --540-* color primitive with its label; semanticColors is a list of groups of --color-* tokens, each item naming the --540-* primitive it takes in light and in dark, and its usage; textStyles has one entry per text style with its key, label, tokenPrefix, mobile and desktop size in px, weight and weight name, line height, letter spacing and usage, and every tokenPrefix has the four tokens <prefix>-size, <prefix>-weight, <prefix>-line-height and <prefix>-letter-spacing; effectTokens lists the --gradient-* and --filter-* tokens, each with the primitive it takes in light and in dark; spacingTokens (--space-*), paddingTokens (--padding-*), gridTokens (--grid-*), sizeTokens (--size-*) and radiusTokens (--radius-*) list the measure tokens with their label and, for some, their usage and their mobile and desktop value in px. Every token name, light alias and dark alias the manifest names is a custom property declared in the token CSS files primitives.css, semantic-color.css, semantic-typography.css or semantic-measure.css.
specs.name: Design tokens

specs.description: The piece renderer (scripts/render: index.mjs, core.mjs, parse.mjs, rules.mjs and spelling.mjs) turns a talk written with tags into one self-contained HTML page. renderTalk(source, {pieces, baseDir, lang, origin}) throws 'renderTalk needs the pieces folder' when pieces is not given; otherwise it reads pieces/manifest.json and returns {html, version, components, islands, scripts, warnings}, where version is the manifest's version, islands lists the island components the page hydrates and scripts says whether the page carries any script. The page has set to lang, else to the talk's own language, else 'es'; its head has and the talk's ; the component CSS is inlined in one <style> with every font of manifest.base.fonts embedded as a data:font/woff2;base64 URL, and every image is embedded as a base64 data URL. A talk made only of static components gives a page with no <script> and no <ds-island>; a talk with islands such as Deck, Steps and Statements gives a page that ships their scripts inline and wraps each island in <ds-island>; inside Steps, a Step's content that is itself a component or SVG is passed as encoded props ({$el, p}) and plain copy as a {$slot}. A talk may also be a page for the browser runtime, its tags inside one <script type="text/rev">: it renders to the same HTML as the plain tags, its data-lang gives the language unless lang is given, errors point to the line and column of the file, and the renderer throws a TagError when there is more than one such block ('only one <script type="text/rev"> per page') or content outside it ('the whole talk goes inside it'). A syntax problem is not collected: parse (parse.mjs) throws at the first one it meets (an unknown entity, a comment or a tag never closed, a malformed or repeated attribute, a closing tag that does not match the open one), and prepareTalk (core.mjs) throws it alone as a TagError '<origin> has 1 problem:'. Once the document parses, every problem prepareTalk finds is collected and thrown together as one TagError '<origin> has <n> problem(s):' with one line per problem: an unknown tag, with the nearest known tag as 'did you mean'; a value outside a prop's options ('<prop> is one of …, not "<value>"'); an attribute the component does not take; plain HTML other than the phrasing tags strong, em, b, i, code, small, sub, sup, br and a (with href); a field a JSON prop does not have; a component that cannot be used from a tag; a missing required prop; content in a component that takes none; a remote image ('points to a remote image') or an image file that does not exist ('image not found'); and, inside a Schema drawing (rev-schema and rev-schema-layer), a class outside the Schema vocabulary, an SVG attribute outside the allowed list such as fill, or a <rev-…> component. A photo of the image library is written biblioteca:<id>: it is embedded from the pieces folder, an id not in manifest.images is a problem that suggests the nearest id, and the same library photo used more than once gives a warning 'biblioteca:<id> is used <n> times'. The renderer also warns, without failing: when a static wrapper cuts a component off its Steps; when one stop shape passes 30 % of the content stops ('<k> of <n> content stops (<p> %)', naming those stops), only when the deck has at least 5 content stops (MIN_STOPS_FOR_SHARE); when two stops in a row have the same shape whatever their copy ('two stops in a row with the same shape'); both checks (checkVariety) look only at the direct children of <rev-deck>, and the content stops are those children leaving out the frame stops rev-cover, rev-block-title and rev-closing; about a big photo with a sentence under it; and when the text beside a photo is aligned to the start. In a Spanish talk (the default) checkSpelling gives one warning per word that neither the Spanish nor the English dictionary nor the 540 word list (WORDS_FILE, render/palabras-540.txt) knows, quoting the word, saying how many times it appears when more than once and adding up to three Spanish suggestions; capitalized words, acronyms, code-like words and words shorter than three letters are skipped, as is the copy inside <code>; a talk in another language is not spell-checked.
specs.name: Piece rendering
